Roofing in Forney, Texas

Forney has added houses faster than almost any city in the country, and most of its roofs are young. One free number reaches an independent roofing company that takes Forney calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 Forney registration and permits
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas

Diamond Creek, April 3, 2012

With so many families arriving since 2012, plenty of Forney homeowners may not know about the day a tornado crossed the edge of town. Roofing in Forney, TX is worth looking at with that day in mind.

During the North Texas outbreak of April 3, 2012, a tornado touched down near Forney, southwest of US 80, and stayed inside Kaufman County for its whole life. The National Weather Service office in Fort Worth rated it EF-3, with winds estimated at 150 mph, a path about 8 miles long and up to about 150 yards wide.

The heaviest damage was in the Diamond Creek subdivision northeast of Forney, where two houses were destroyed and several others were heavily damaged. The tornado also damaged the roof of Crosby Elementary School, and a car from the school's parking lot was carried about 300 yards into a field. Seven people were hurt; no one died.

The fastest-growing city in the country, for a while

Since that storm, Forney has been transformed. Using census estimates, the Dallas Business Journal found that Forney led the nation in population growth from 2020 to 2023, at 51.2 percent, reaching about 35,470 residents by July 2023. The Census Bureau's own list put Forney tenth among fast-growing U.S. cities for the year ending July 2023, at 10.4 percent.

For roofs, that means a city full of first roofs on new houses. Young roofs still need attention. Hail does not care how old the shingles are, a builder's roof can have flashing or ventilation mistakes that show up only after a few seasons, and many new owners are unsure whether the builder's warranty or their homeowners policy is the first call. A roofer can tell you what it finds; your builder and insurer can tell you what they cover.

Forney's registration and permit rules, step by step

  1. The roofer registers with the city. Forney requires every contractor working inside city limits to register, and no permit is issued until it does. The fee is $30 per license.
  2. Registration expires on December 31. Forney registrations cover the current calendar year only. Early in a new year, ask whether the roofer has renewed.
  3. The permit comes before the work. The city says permits must be obtained before improvements or alterations, and its fee schedule lists re-roofing.
  4. Everything runs through MyGov. Registration and permit applications are filed online in the city's MyGov portal.
  5. Start within 180 days. The residential application says a permit becomes void if work has not begun within 180 days of issue.

Rules and fees change. Check the details for your job with Forney's building inspection office before work begins.

Three power companies, one rule: stay clear

A storm that damages a roof often brings down lines too. In Forney, which utility to call depends on your address.

ProviderPart of Forney it serves, per the Forney EDC
OncorThe largest provider: downtown, north of US 80 and the Gateway area
Trinity Valley Electric CooperativeSouthern Forney near I-20 and around Forney High School
Farmers Electric CooperativeListed as the third supplier; check your bill

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor, Trinity Valley Electric Cooperative or Farmers Electric Cooperative, whichever serves your address, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Why Forney homeowners call

Hail on a nearly new roof

Owners of houses only a few years old are often surprised by hail damage and unsure whether it is worth a claim. A roofer's written findings help with that conversation.

A leak in a new house

Stains around a vent or skylight in a young home can point to an installation detail. Ask the roofer to photograph it so you can raise it with the builder.

Homeowners association approval

If your subdivision has an HOA, note that Texas Property Code 202.011 limits an association's power to ban wind and hail resistant shingles that look like the approved ones.

Paperwork for a fast-changing city

With registration renewing every January, homeowners want a roofer that keeps its Forney paperwork current and files permits in MyGov.

Questions worth asking a Forney roofer

  • Is your Forney registration renewed for this calendar year?
  • Will the re-roof permit be in MyGov before you start, and can I have the number?
  • On a newer house, will you photograph anything that looks like an installation problem so I can show the builder?
  • What wind and hail ratings does the shingle you recommend carry, and will it satisfy my HOA?
  • Will your liability carrier send the certificate to me directly?
  • What exactly does your workmanship warranty promise, and is it written into the contract?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. Forney roofing questions

Do roofing companies have to register with the City of Forney?

Yes. Forney says every contractor completing work inside city limits must be registered with the city, and a contractor cannot pull a permit until it is. Registration is done online through MyGov, costs $30 per license, and runs for the calendar year only, January through December. So a registration from last year does not cover this year's job. Ask the roofer to confirm it renewed.

Does a new roof in Forney TX need a permit?

Forney says building permits must be obtained before improvements or alterations are made to a property, and its master fee schedule carries a re-roofing line. Applications go through MyGov. The residential application warns that a permit becomes void if work does not start within 180 days, so a roofer should apply close to the install date. Ask for the permit number in writing.

Who do I call about a downed power line in Forney?

Call 911 and the utility that serves your address. The Forney Economic Development Corporation lists three: Oncor, the largest, covering downtown and the area north of US 80; Trinity Valley Electric Cooperative in southern Forney near I-20; and Farmers Electric Cooperative. Your bill names your provider. Stay far from any line on or near the roof.

Has a tornado ever hit Forney?

Yes. On April 3, 2012, the National Weather Service rated a tornado near Forney EF-3, with winds estimated at 150 mph along a path about 8 miles long. It touched down southwest of US 80 and did its worst damage in the Diamond Creek subdivision northeast of town, destroying two homes and badly damaging several more. The storm damage guide covers what to do after a storm.

What happens when I call the line about roofing in Forney?

An automated assistant answers for DFW Expert Roofers, which is a free phone line, at any hour. Say it is a roof, describe the problem and give your Forney address. The call is passed to an independent, locally owned roofer covering Kaufman County. That roofer quotes and does any work, and you pay it. Roofers can pay the line for the referral. How it works.
